name: Soy Isoflavones
aliases: soy isoflavones, soya isoflavones, soybean isoflavones, isoflavones, genistein, daidzein, glycitein, soy isoflavone extract, soya isoflavone extract
what_is: Naturally occurring soy compounds, including genistein, daidzein and glycitein, that belong to the isoflavone family and can interact with oestrogen receptors.
why_botia: BOTIA flags them in the Woman layer because isoflavones have been specifically assessed in female life-stage contexts, while the evidence does not support inferring a benefit, harm or hormonal effect from the ingredient name alone.
can_1: Identify explicitly declared soy isoflavones, isoflavone extracts and common named isoflavones on the label.
can_2: Trigger the Woman information layer and distinguish an explicitly declared isoflavone ingredient from ordinary soy ingredients that do not state an isoflavone amount.
cannot_1: Calculate the isoflavone dose from a generic soy ingredient when the label gives no quantitative information.
cannot_2: Predict hormonal, menopausal or other clinical effects for an individual user.
